stories.headline: Apple and Intel Reach Preliminary Deal for Intel Foundry to Make Some Apple Chips

key_facts.fact: Apple and Intel reached a preliminary agreement in recent months for Intel to manufacture some of the chips that power Apple devices, after more than a year of intensive talks.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple and Intel have reached a preliminary agreement for Intel to manufacture some of the chips that power Apple devices, according to people familiar with the matter. Intensive talks between the two companies have been ongoing for more than a year, and they hammered out a formal deal in recent months.

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration played a major role in bringing Apple to the table; President Trump personally advocated for Intel to Tim Cook in a White House meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: Per the WSJ report, the US government played a key role in the Apple deal. 'President Trump personally advocated for Intel to Cook in a meeting at the White House, according to people familiar with the matter.'

key_facts.fact: If completed, the deal would end Apple's sole reliance on TSMC for its most advanced chips and represent the most notable vote of confidence yet for Intel's foundry business.
key_facts.excerpt: Landing an Apple contract will give Intel a steady stream of demand from one of the world's largest consumer electronics companies, bolstering both its reputation and a manufacturing business that has fallen behind TSMC in recent years. For Apple, a deal with Intel could mean a diversification in manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: Intel shares are up more than 200% in 2026 amid the foundry turnaround under CEO Lip-Bu Tan; the US government became Intel's largest shareholder last year.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel has spent the last year signing deals with the U.S. government and securing investments from AI chip giant Nvidia and SoftBank amid a push from CEO Lip-Bu Tan to turn the chipmaker around. The U.S. government, which became Intel's largest shareholder last year under a deal with its CEO Lip-Bu Tan, played a major role in bringing Apple to the negotiating table.

key_facts.fact: Analysts expect Apple is most likely to wait for Intel's next 18A-P process node, which could scale next year, rather than today's 18A node.
key_facts.excerpt: If (and when) the Apple Intel deal happens, @BenBajarin says it'll be for 18A-P. That could scale next year, spelling the end of an era for Apple's sole reliance on TSMC.

key_facts.fact: Apple may start with less advanced chips such as Apple Watch S-series or networking parts before moving to flagship A-series or M-series silicon.
key_facts.excerpt: It seems more likely that Apple would start by manufacturing chips that are a little further behind the bleeding edge, such as S-series chips for Apple Watch or the company's N or C series networking chips.

stories.headline: Apollo and Blackstone in Talks With Broadcom on ~$35B Private Credit Deal to Fund AI Chip Push

key_facts.fact: Apollo Global Management and Blackstone are among private credit lenders in talks with Broadcom over roughly $35 billion in financing, which would be one of the largest private credit deals ever.
key_facts.excerpt: Apollo Global Management and Blackstone are reported to be negotiating roughly $35 billion in financing with Broadcom to support the chipmaker's production of AI-focused processors. The proposed transaction would be among the largest private credit deals on record.

key_facts.fact: The financing would fund development and production of Broadcom's AI-specific chips and is described as preliminary, with terms still under negotiation.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom is said to be seeking funds specifically to support production of chips designed for AI applications, aligning capital plans with the company's recent commercial agreements in the AI ecosystem. All reported discussions about the roughly $35 billion financing are described as preliminary and negotiable.

key_facts.fact: The talks come after Broadcom disclosed multi-year agreements with Google and an expanded TPU partnership involving Google and Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: Terms remain under negotiation, and the talks come after Broadcom disclosed multi-year agreements with Google and an expanded partnership with Google and Anthropic for TPU-based AI capacity.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg first reported the Apollo/Blackstone talks on May 8, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Apollo And Blackstone Weigh $35 Billion Financing For Broadcom- Bloomberg News

stories.headline: Cerebras to Raise IPO Price Range to $125-$135 After 20x Oversubscription

key_facts.fact: Cerebras is set to raise its IPO price range as soon as Monday from $115-$125 to $125-$135 per share after orders exceeded 20 times the shares available, sources told Bloomberg.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: Cerebras plans to raise its IPO price range from $115-$125 per share to $125-$135 after drawing orders for more than 20x the number of shares available

key_facts.fact: The company is offering 28 million Class A shares plus a 4.2 million-share underwriter option; at the original $115-$125 range it could be valued up to $26.6 billion and raise up to $3.5 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: AI chip company Cerebras is aiming for a valuation of up to $26.62 billion in its US initial public offering, according to Reuters. The company is offering 28 million shares of Class A common stock priced between $115 and $125 each, which could help it raise up to $3.5 billion, and make it the largest tech IPO of 2026 so far. Underwriters have a 30-day option to purchase an additional 4.2 million shares.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras' February 2026 Series H led by Tiger Global priced the company at $23 billion, with AMD, Benchmark, Fidelity, Altimeter and Coatue participating; the IPO range implies a ~15% step-up in three months.
key_facts.excerpt: Its most recent private round, a $1 billion Series H led by Tiger Global in February 2026, valued it at $23 billion, with Benchmark, Fidelity, Altimeter, AMD, and Coatue also participating. The IPO range implies a roughly 15% step-up from that private valuation in just three months.

key_facts.fact: CEO Andrew Feldman is not selling shares; he will hold 10.3 million shares post-IPO worth up to $1.28 billion at the prior high end.
key_facts.excerpt: CNBC notes that chief executive Andrew Feldman, the company's co-founder, is not selling shares in the IPO; he will hold 10.3 million shares post-deal, worth as much as $1.28bn at the high end.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras' lead banks for the deal are Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays and UBS; the offering would be the largest semiconductor IPO since Arm's 2023 debut.
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras Systems opened its IPO roadshow on Monday at a $40 billion target valuation, with up to $4 billion in proceeds, after the deal's lead banks — Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays, and UBS — booked more than $10 billion in indications of interest in advance of pricing. Pricing is expected mid-May. The company will list under the ticker CBRS. The IPO would be the largest U.S. AI-infrastructure listing of 2026 and the largest semiconductor IPO since Arm's 2023 debut.

stories.headline: Honeywell-Backed Quantinuum Files Public S-1 for Nasdaq IPO Under Ticker QNT

key_facts.fact: Quantinuum publicly filed a Form S-1 with the SEC on May 8, 2026 for an IPO of Class A common stock and intends to list on Nasdaq under ticker QNT.
key_facts.excerpt: Honeywell (NASDAQ: HON) today announced that Quantinuum, a leading, full-stack quantum computing company, has publicly filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the 'SEC') relating to a proposed initial public offering of shares of its Class A common stock... Quantinuum intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol 'QNT.'

key_facts.fact: Quantinuum's net revenue and net loss for the three months ended March 31, 2026 were $5.2 million and $136.6 million, respectively, vs. $19.1 million and $30.5 million a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Our net revenue and net loss for the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $5.2 million and $136.6 million, respectively, compared to $19.1 million and $30.5 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025.

key_facts.fact: For full-year 2025, Quantinuum reported net revenue of $30.9 million and a net loss of $192.6 million; cash and equivalents stood at $677.0 million as of March 31, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Our net revenue and net loss for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $30.9 million and $192.6 million, respectively. For the year ended December 31, 2024, our net revenue and net loss was $23.0 million and $144.1 million, respectively. Additionally, as of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, our cash and cash equivalents were $677.0 million and $762.6 million.

key_facts.fact: Quantinuum raised about $600 million last year at a $10 billion pre-money valuation, with J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley leading the offering.
key_facts.excerpt: Quantinuum, a Honeywell-backed quantum computing company, filed on May 8 to go public on Nasdaq under 'QNT,' with J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley leading the deal... Quantinuum raised about $600 million last year at a $10 billion pre-money valuation.

key_facts.fact: Quantinuum was formed in 2021 by merging Honeywell Quantum Solutions with UK-based Cambridge Quantum; Honeywell will remain a strategic customer post-IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: Quantinuum was formed in 2021 through the combination of Honeywell Quantum Solutions and Cambridge Quantum, uniting innovative quantum hardware expertise with advanced quantum software capabilities... Honeywell has indicated its intent to remain a strategic customer and partner following this offering.

key_facts.fact: Bookings totaled $1.3 million in Q1 2026 and $79.3 million for full-year 2025, with active engagements across pharmaceuticals, materials, financial services, and government.
key_facts.excerpt: Bookings were $1.3 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026 compared to $1.9 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025. Bookings were $79.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2025.

stories.headline: Chinese Humanoid Robotics Startup Robotera Raises $200M+ Led by SF Group

key_facts.fact: Beijing-based humanoid robotics company Robotera announced on May 8 it raised over $200 million in a new round led by logistics giant SF Group, following a 1 billion yuan strategic round in March.
key_facts.excerpt: BEIJING, May 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Following its RMB 1 billion strategic round in March, robotics company ROBOTERA has raised over USD 200 million in a new financing round led by SF Group.

key_facts.fact: The round drew financial investors including HSG (Sequoia China), IDG Capital, Hillhouse Investment, CICC Capital, plus industrial partners KENGIC, Dongfeng Asset Investment, ICBC Capital, and China Unicom-affiliated funds; investor demand significantly exceeded the initial target.
key_facts.excerpt: The round also saw participation from leading financial investors including HSG, IDG Capital, Hillhouse Investment, CICC Capital, Jingming Capital, SparkEdge Capital, Luxin Venture Capital Group, Unite Pioneers Capital, and Longqi Investment; alongside major industrial partners such as KENGIC, Dongfeng Asset Investment, ICBC Capital, and funds affiliated with China Unicom... Investor demand significantly exceeded the initial fundraising target.

key_facts.fact: Robotera says it has reached the first product-market fit in embodied intelligence, with deployments across more than ten logistics centers with China Post and SF Group, and started thousand-unit deliveries in Q2 2026 with growth exceeding 300%.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has achieved the first product-market fit (PMF) in the embodied intelligence sector, with deployments across more than ten logistics centers in collaboration with China Post and SF Group. In Q2 2026, ROBOTERA initiated thousand-unit deliveries, with growth exceeding 300%.

key_facts.fact: Founded in August 2023 by Chen Jianyu, Robotera makes the L7 full-size bipedal humanoid (~171 cm), the STAR 1 model, the ERA-42 embodied AI model, and dexterous direct-drive hands.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in August 2023 by Chen Jianyu, Robotera is a humanoid robotics company. Its offers include: L7 (Full-Size Bipedal): Their flagship model, standing about 171 cm (5'7') tall. STAR 1: A humanoid tested in extreme environments like the Gobi Desert and the Great Wall of China. ERA-42 Large Model: An end-to-end 'embodied AI' model. Dexterous Hands: Their direct-drive robotic hands (like the XHand) are designed for precision tasks in logistics and manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: More than 95% of Robotera's core hardware components are developed in-house, spanning actuation systems and humanoid platforms.
key_facts.excerpt: Beyond deployment, ROBOTERA has built a fully in-house robotics hardware system, with over 95% of core components developed internally, spanning actuation systems and humanoid platforms, forming a robust foundation for real-world mobility and manipulation tasks.

stories.headline: Top Motherboard Brands Slash 2026 Targets 24%-37% as AI Chips Squeeze Consumer PC Market

key_facts.fact: Asus, Gigabyte, MSI and ASRock have all lowered 2026 motherboard shipment targets, with declines ranging from ~24% to ~37% versus 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: ASUS: 15.0 million (2025) → ~10.0 million (2026 target) | ~-33% YoY. GIGABYTE: 11.5 million → 8.0-8.5 million | ~-26% to -30%. MSI: 11.0 million → 8.4 million | ~-24%. ASRock: 4.3 million → 2.7 million | ~-37%.

key_facts.fact: Asus is on track for its lowest motherboard shipments since the company's 2008 split, projected to ship around 10 million boards in 2026 versus 15 million in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: ASUS, which stays at the top of motherboard sales for years, is expected to ship around 5 million motherboards in the first half of 2026, but weaker second-half demand could put its full-year result close to 10 million units. Digitimes says this would be ASUS's lowest motherboard shipment level since its 2008 split.

key_facts.fact: DRAM and CPU shortages have pushed memory to over 30% of a typical PC's bill of materials, up from roughly 15% historically; PC makers have responded with 10%-20% price increases or weaker configurations.
key_facts.excerpt: The DigiTimes report suggests that severe shortages of DRAM and CPUs have driven prices so high that DIY PC building is being suppressed. Memory kits now account for over 30% of total PC build costs, up from approximately 15% in previous years.

key_facts.fact: Intel and AMD are prioritizing high-margin server CPUs (Xeon, EPYC) over consumer parts, exacerbating DIY PC supply shortages.
key_facts.excerpt: Chipmakers like Intel and AMD are reportedly prioritizing production of high-profit server processors such as Xeon and EPYC chips instead of consumer CPUs. As a result, desktop and laptop processors are facing supply shortages and price increases.

key_facts.fact: AMD CEO Lisa Su has said gaming demand is expected to decline in the second half of 2026 due to component cost pressure; brands are pivoting toward AI server platforms to offset weakness.
key_facts.excerpt: Even AMD's CEO, Dr. Lisa Su, has stated that gaming demand is expected to decline in the second half of 2026 due to out-of-control component costs. However, companies will be able to offset these losses by pivoting towards more lucrative AI datacentre sales.
